about: Every number on these slides and in their speaker notes, with its source. The measured results come from our evaluation tasks and published evidence.

claims.number: 314 repositories about agent memory created on GitHub in the 48 hours to October 31, 2026 at 23:27 UTC
claims.source: GitHub search 'agent memory created:2026-10-29T23:27:00Z..2026-10-31T23:27:00Z', measured at 2026-10-31T23:27:59Z, with the response kept in the scan’s record; the memory-systems feed’s scan of October 31 at 23:27 UTC on a local copy of Tessera.

claims.number: 587 repositories gathered; the first four in feed rank, as of October 31, for Python, MIT licence, runs locally have 14,358, 4,303, 4,085, 3,858 stars
claims.source: The feed’s stored Task Objects from the scan of October 31 at 23:27 UTC, rendered on Agora’s feed page, which links the scan’s record.

claims.number: 705 of 739 public repos in the event directory scanned into Tasks and Task Objects
claims.source: The same scan as the records slide: a deterministic scan (hackscan 1.2.0) cloned each repo shallowly and read its tree without running any code, on October 29, 2026; 34 failed (24 empty, 5 not found or private, 5 timed out). Aggregate counts only.

claims.number: 80 seed packs in one library, with 1,520 Task Objects, 490 Task templates and 45 worked examples
claims.source: A count of the packs in the seed-pack library's README as of October 31, 2026. They are proposals and validated examples: none is installed, imported, admitted or activated.

claims.number: {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}}: exact match 93.3% to 99.3% on our 150-task tool-call evaluation, +6.0 points, 95% CI +2.0 to +10.7; promotion rule 12 of 12
claims.source: QLoRA on Kaggle’s free notebook GPUs, scored on a fresh 150-row test recorded before scoring. A fresh reload reproduced its outputs. The rule said promote; nothing has been promoted or admitted. The run record is published with this deck’s evidence.

claims.number: {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}}, as memory: closed-book exact match 0.0% to 62.5% on a 120-row test fixed before scoring, with 0 added tokens
claims.source: QLoRA on two free Kaggle T4 GPUs, October 31, 2026: recalling the library’s Task Objects and workflows from the model’s own weights, with nothing added to the prompt. A promoted candidate only; nothing has been admitted or deployed.

claims.number: 10/10 agent processes finished their shared tasks in one wave
claims.source: Ten native Pi processes on our evaluation tasks, October 29, 2026. Earlier waves of 7/10 and 3/3 are also on record.

claims.number: 100/100 protocol clients in 25.7 seconds, with no rate-limit rejections
claims.source: A short protocol load test on October 29, 2026: 25.663 seconds and no HTTP 429. Expected write conflicts did occur. Not 100 separate agent programs.

claims.number: 6 agent programs each finished a scoped task; 6 of 14 attempts passed
claims.source: OpenCode, Pi, Hermes, {{model:muse-code}}, {{model:nanomuse}} and OpenClaw in narrow lifecycle tests, with every failure recorded. A seventh program, Claude Code, passed a separate test later.

claims.number: 0 model tokens while compiled code recipes run
claims.source: Compiled recipes run as plain code; six local deterministic runs are recorded. Making or checking a recipe can still use a model.

claims.number: 16 of 16 recorded steps recheck for the film’s production run
claims.source: The film’s production ran as 16 claimed Tasks of 7 kinds on a local Tessera store, with no model calls. The published bundle’s verify.py rechecks every record with Tessera’s rule, checks that 142 of 161 input pins are outputs of earlier recorded Tasks (the rest are setup Task Objects), and ties all 12 published files to their records. The store itself is not public.

claims.number: 705 of 739 public repos in the event directory scanned into Tasks and Task Objects
claims.source: A deterministic scan (hackscan 1.2.0) cloned each repo shallowly and read its tree without running any code, on October 29, 2026; 34 failed (24 empty, 5 not found or private, 5 timed out). Aggregate counts only.

claims.number: 58.9% of scanned repos reference Meta's model API; 4.3% use MCP
claims.source: 415 of 705 scanned repos contain the text api.meta.ai, and 30 show an MCP signal (an SDK dependency, server code, tool definitions or client config). Mentions are text matches, not evidence of use.
